entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK this package builds against declares it and the release has no such symbol, so the port has to export it. Its precondition is the header's own - "It is an error to call this function when multi-pass encoding has not been enabled by setting kVTCompressionPropertyKey_MultiPassStorage" - and that precondition is ASKED rather than assumed: VTSessionCopyProperty with kVTCompressionPropertyKey_MultiPassStorage answers NULL on a session that was never given one, because the property arrived with iOS 9 and the 6.1.3 encoder does not have it relcheck places these three on the ladder at 7.0 and that is the value the row carries
entries.effect: kVTParameterErr (-12902) when the session holds no multi-pass storage, which is the header's error case; kVTVideoEncoderNotAvailableNowErr (-12915) if a session somehow did hold one, because the 6.1.3 encoder knows nothing about pass boundaries and would not honour the call either
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTCompressionSession.h:358 for the declaration and VTCompressionProperties.h:940 for the precondition; the query is VTSessionCopyProperty, which the 16.4 SDK declares at VTSession.h:112 and the release implements

entries.reason: same precondition and same query as -VTCompressionSessionBeginPass: the header says it is an error to call EndPass when multi-pass was never enabled, and VTSessionCopyProperty answers NULL for such a session relcheck places these three on the ladder at 7.0 and that is the value the row carries
entries.effect: kVTParameterErr (-12902) in the header's error case, and *furtherPassesRequestedOut is NOT written on either path - the header makes the caller read it only after a success, and writing false on an error would let a caller that forgets the status end its loop believing the encoder wanted no more passes
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTCompressionSession.h:380 for the declaration, and the same header's own wording that the caller may pass NULL to skip the evaluation step

entries.reason: the header names two error conditions - multi-pass never enabled, and EndPass not having asked for another pass - and BOTH are kVTParameterErr, so there is one outcome and not two. The first is the one that runs and is asked of the session; the second is unreachable on this release, since no pass ever ends here relcheck places these three on the ladder at 7.0 and that is the value the row carries
entries.effect: kVTParameterErr (-12902), with neither out parameter written - the header makes both non-null and reads them only after a success
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTCompressionSession.h:398 for the declaration and the two conditions in the same header's @discussion

entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK declares it and the release has no such symbol, so the port exports it. It exists to hand the caller the encoded frame through a block passed per call, and the release cannot do that: the header requires a session created with a NULL callback ("Cannot be called with a session created with a VTCompressionOutputCallback"), the callback is fixed at VTCompressionSessionCreate time, and there is no VTCompressionSessionSetOutputCallback in the release - measured over its own symbol table, one hit for _VTCompressionSessionCreate and _VTCompressionSessionEncodeFrame and ZERO for _VTCompressionSessionSetOutputCallback - nor in the 26.2 SDK. The frame therefore cannot reach the block, and this entry point says so with a status instead of encoding the frame and dropping it, which would be work the caller cannot see
entries.effect: kVTVideoEncoderNotAvailableNowErr (-12915) and NO work done: the frame is not encoded, so nothing is encoded and thrown away and the caller's block is not called with a hole where a frame should have been. A caller that needs frames on this release is not stuck: it creates the session with a VTCompressionOutputCallback and calls VTCompressionSessionEncodeFrame, which the release exports and which this port does not touch. This entry point is the one that cannot work here and it reports that rather than failing quietly
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTCompressionSession.h:313 for the declaration and the "Cannot be called" line in the same header's @discussion; the absence of a setter measured with tools/corpus/dump-cache.lua over $HOME/.charon/dyld/6.1.3/dyld_shared_cache_armv7 on 2026-10-03

entries.reason: the same cause on the decompression side, measured the same way: the header requires a session created with a NULL callback ("Cannot be called with a session created with a VTDecompressionOutputCallbackRecord"), _VTDecompressionSessionCreate and _VTDecompressionSessionDecodeFrame are in the 6.1.3 symbol table and _VTDecompressionSessionSetOutputCallback is not, in the release or in the 26.2 SDK
entries.effect: kVTVideoDecoderNotAvailableNowErr (-12913) and NO work done: the frame is not decoded and the caller's block is not called. The notification route does not deliver it either, and that was measured rather than assumed: _kVTDecompressionSessionNotification_FrameDecodeCompleted IS in the 6.1.3 symbol table, but it is declared in no C header of the 16.4 SDK, the 26.2 SDK or the host - only in the three VideoToolbox.tbd export tables - so there is no declared contract for what it carries, and kVTDecompressionSessionFrameDecodeNotificationUserInfoKey, the key that would name the frame, is not in the 6.1.3 symbol table at all. A caller that needs frames creates the session with a VTDecompressionOutputCallbackRecord and calls VTDecompressionSessionDecodeFrame

entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK declares it and the release has no such symbol, so the port exports it. The header's whole documented behaviour is the FILE: created "using a temporary file", fileURL names it, NULL means "the video toolbox will pick a unique temporary file name", and kVTMultiPassStorageCreationOption_DoNotDelete keeps it. Every one of those is measured against the host's own VideoToolbox rather than assumed: a fresh path gives status 0, a session and a created file; NULL gives status 0 and a session; a path whose file ALREADY EXISTS gives kVTMultiPassStorageInvalidErr (-12214) and no session; and a path whose parent directory does not exist gives -17913 with no file created
entries.effect: a real file with the header's lifecycle: a fresh path is created and deleted on finalize unless kVTMultiPassStorageCreationOption_DoNotDelete is set (both measured on the host: gone without the option, present with it), a path that already exists is refused with kVTMultiPassStorageInvalidErr (-12214) and left untouched, NULL picks a unique name in the temporary directory. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it writes no private header into the file. Apple's writes 20 bytes at Create and the header says the contents are "private to the video encoder", so a file this port writes is not readable by a real encoder and nothing in this port reads it either - the 6.1.3 encoder never sees a multi-pass storage because kVTCompressionPropertyKey_MultiPassStorage arrived with iOS 9. The lifecycle is what the header specifies and what a caller can observe; the contents are Apple's and are not reproduced A path whose PARENT DIRECTORY does not exist answers -17913, the value Apple's own Create gives and the one this port now answers instead of kVTAllocationFailedErr. -17913 is named in no header on this machine - not VideoToolbox's VTErrors.h, and nothing under any framework in the 16.4 SDK, the 26.2 SDK or the macOS SDK - so it is spelled as a named constant in VTMultiPassStorage9_0.m with its source beside it rather than as a bare literal, and the owning framework is recorded as not identified rather than guessed at. The parent directory is checked on its own so the measured code answers the measured condition and is not stretched over create failures nobody measured
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTMultiPassStorage.h:61 for the declaration, :54 for kVTMultiPassStorageCreationOption_DoNotDelete and :72 for the option itself; all five answers measured against /System/Library/Frameworks/VideoToolbox.framework on 2026-10-03
